3. The defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying the arterial statements made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable in its present form and was barred by limitation. The industry of defendant was a small scale industry. As per gazette notification, interest chargeable in a small scale industry was 10% P.A. But, in the instant case, the plaintiff-bank used to charge interest sometimes @ 12% and sometimes @ 15% compound interest per annum. The defendant took loan of taka 14,00,000'00, but no loan agreement was executed. The plaintiff charged compound interest violating the instruction of the ministry of finance. After obtaining loan, the defendant incurred loss in manufacturing bricks from 1994 to 1996 due to heavy rainfall. Besides, due to frequent hartal, production of bricks was disturbed. The defendant informed such facts to the plaintiff-Bank who assured it to pay the principal amount by installments and on the basis of such assurance, the defendant deposited taka 2,33,58T 00 as 10% of total dues as down payment for waiver of interest But the plaintiff did not consider the application of the defendant and filed the suit, and as such, it was not entitled to get any relief in the suit and the same was liable to be dismissed. 

 6. Mr. Manmunoor Rashid, learned Advocate, placing the relevant statements made in the plaint submitted that the loan advanced to the defendant was secured by mortgaging its property. Therefore, limitation for filing the suit in the instant case would be governed by article 132 of the Limitation Act, but the High Court Division on misconception of the facts and circumstances of the case as made out in the plaint relied upon article 57 of the Limitation Act and wrongly held that the suit having not been filed within the 3(three) years was barred by limitation.
